subject: Preflight: tenant IO contracts, BIOS tuning, and PV reconciliation

Hi Hannah —

- Recommended BIOS settings (C-states, power profile, SR-IOV) for stable NVMe throughput
- Nodeclass sizing guidance when we want mixed GPU and CPU pools (in particular, best-effort vs guaranteed storage QoS)
- PV reclaim/eviction policy defaults and how Redwood’s KV/cache interacts with local NVMe vs network blockstore

I attached our current site inventory and the checklist you provided. Can we get a concise tech snapshot we can attach to the procurement package?

Also looping Alex (infra) for any OS/kernel constraints.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Preflight questions before on-prem kickoff

Tara —

Appreciate the inventory and the clear asks. I sketched a short tech snapshot below you can paste into procurement. We should also do a 30–45 minute call tomorrow to walk through any site-specific constraints. Suggested times: 10am or 2pm PT.

Quick snapshot (for procurement):
- BIOS/firmware: Disable deep C-states (C3+), set CPU power policy to "performance", enable UEFI NVMe driver, and enable SR-IOV on NICs that will be used for RDMA/fast-path. Recommended microcode >= 2024.12.
- Kernel: RHEL 8.8+/Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS with iommu=pt for SR-IOV, transparent hugepages=never. We recommend stock distro kernels with hotpatching; we’ll call out a required perfpatch for older NIC firmwares.
- Node classes:
  * gpu-large: 8xA100 (or 4xH100), 1.5TB NVMe local scratch, 512GB RAM — reserved QoS, local PV reclaim policy: Retain + periodic snapshot to blockstore.
  * gpu-shared: 4xA100, 750GB NVMe, 256GB RAM — best-effort QoS, ephemeral cache on local NVMe with backing backup to NFS/Blockstore.
  * control/infra: 4cpu/32GB, small NVMe for kubelet and logs, dedicated NIC on management VLAN.
- Storage: Use local NVMe for KV/cache and ephemeral model slices; daily async snapshot to encrypted network blockstore (S3-backed blockstore or iSCSI target). Ensure LVM thin pool not used for high-write model caches (preferred raw partitions or XFS on dm-crypt).
- K8s eviction: kubelet eviction thresholds tuned to false-positive-resistant values (memory.available < 200Mi not used for GPU nodes), and a custom eviction hook that flushes KV cache to blockstore on OOM warnings.
- Networking: Separate control, data (model traffic), and mgmt VLANs; BGP egress for multi-datacenter routing if applicable. Recommend jumbo frames on model-network.

I’ll attach a single-page PDF per your ask. Marissa, Dylan — any additions on storage IO caps or preflight tests we should call out?

If tomorrow 10am works for you Tara, I’ll send a calendar invite.

— Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-tech-snapshot-obsidian.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Adding a few concrete IO validation steps we do during the field kit:

1) NVMe baseline: run fio profiles that simulate continuous 128KB sequential and random workloads for 4 hours to capture sustained P99 latency and steady-state throughput. Target: P99 < 3ms for sequential reads on model shard volumes.
2) Write endurance check: flash-erase/workload to validate expected TBW for local sats; report if drives are below spec.
3) Network path: tcpdump + iperf3 between model-net leafs using jumbo frames and simulating 1.5x expected concurrent token flows.
4) KV cache flush test: simulate a 2x workload spike for 20 minutes and validate that KV checkpoints to remote blockstore within 5 minutes of threshold.

Operational notes: prefer XFS on raw partitions with no LVM layer for model cache disks; use dm-crypt with a mounted key from customer KMS if they require HSM-backed keys.

I’ll post the fio job configs to the shared drive link.

-Marissa
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@obsidianhealth.com>

Thanks — the snapshot looks good. A couple clarifying items from our side before the call:

- For the KV cache flush SLA, can you confirm whether the snapshot operation will throttle IO so it doesn’t impact model serving latency? We run some 99th-percentile-sensitive endpoints.
- For encrypted backups, does Redwood require specific blockstore API compatibility, or will standard S3-encrypted targets be supported?

Also 10am PT tomorrow works — please send invite.

— Alex
Infrastructure Lead, Obsidian Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-04-19 15:43 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight questions before on-prem kickoff

Alex/Tara —

Quick answers before the call:
- Snapshot impact: our checkpointer uses IO prioritization and background throttling so snapshots are snapshot-aware; by default it limits bandwidth to 100MB/s per node (configurable). During the call we can show a toggled run with and without throttle so you can see p99 effects.
- Blockstore compatibility: we support S3-compatible encrypted endpoints (customer-managed keys via KMS is supported). For strict HSM-only flows we have a plug that uses KMIP/HSM and iSCSI wrapped volumes — we’ll need to validate with your procurement that HSM deployment is in scope.

Next steps: calendar invite sent for 2027-04-19 10:00 PT (re-sent for your timezone). Deliverables from our side after the call: single-page procurement-ready tech snapshot (attached), fio job outputs, and a short runbook for the onsite validation steps.

See you on the call —
Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
